# Literature Map — persuasion_turn_jailbreak_detect
# Generated: 2026-05-17 by Paper Agent
# Target: EMNLP 2026 Main (ARR May cycle)
# Total entries: 39 (across 8 categories + technical foundation)
# All entries WebSearch-verified unless noted

metadata:
  project: persuasion_turn_jailbreak_detect
  target_venue: EMNLP 2026
  last_updated: "2026-05-17"
  total_papers: 39
  categories:
    - production_safety_systems
    - multi_turn_defenses
    - discourse_analysis
    - computational_persuasion
    - jailbreak_attacks_taxonomies
    - red_teaming
    - annotation_artifacts
    - adaptive_attacks
    - technical_foundation

papers:

  # ============================================================
  # Category 1: Production Multi-Turn Safety Systems (5 papers)
  # ============================================================

  - bibtex_key: inan2023llamaguard
    title: "Llama Guard: LLM-based Input-Output Safeguard for Human-AI Conversations"
    authors: "Inan et al."
    venue: "arXiv preprint"
    year: 2023
    arxiv: "2312.06674"
    category: production_safety_systems
    role: background
    verified: true
    relevance_to_our_work: >
      Foundational production safety classifier. Per-turn input/output guard
      that lacks multi-turn context modeling. DisPeD addresses this gap by
      modeling conversation-level persuasion trajectories.

  - bibtex_key: metallamaguard3_2024
    title: "Llama Guard 3"
    authors: "Meta AI"
    venue: "Meta AI (released with Llama 3.1)"
    year: 2024
    category: production_safety_systems
    role: background
    verified: true
    relevance_to_our_work: >
      Latest iteration of Llama Guard with multilingual support and tool-use
      safety. Still operates per-turn without multi-turn trajectory modeling.
      Baseline comparison target for production safety systems.

  - bibtex_key: zeng2024shieldgemma
    title: "ShieldGemma: Generative AI Content Moderation Based on Gemma"
    authors: "Zeng et al."
    venue: "arXiv preprint"
    year: 2024
    arxiv: "2407.21772"
    category: production_safety_systems
    role: background
    verified: true
    relevance_to_our_work: >
      Google's safety classifier suite (2B/9B/27B). Outperforms Llama Guard
      on public benchmarks. Demonstrates strong per-turn moderation but does
      not model multi-turn attack trajectories.

  - bibtex_key: han2024wildguard
    title: "WildGuard: Open One-Stop Moderation Tools for Safety Risks, Jailbreaks, and Refusals of LLMs"
    authors: "Han et al."
    venue: "NeurIPS 2024"
    year: 2024
    arxiv: "2406.18495"
    category: production_safety_systems
    role: background
    verified: true
    relevance_to_our_work: >
      Allen AI's multi-task safety moderator (prompt harm + response harm +
      refusal detection). Reduces jailbreak ASR from 79.8% to 2.4% on
      single-turn attacks, but multi-turn evasion path remains open.

  - bibtex_key: anthropic2025constitutional
    title: "Constitutional Classifiers: Defending against Universal Jailbreaks across Thousands of Hours of Red Teaming"
    authors: "Anthropic"
    venue: "arXiv preprint"
    year: 2025
    arxiv: "2501.18837"
    category: production_safety_systems
    role: background
    verified: true
    relevance_to_our_work: >
      Anthropic's defense using synthetically-generated training data from
      constitutional rules. Reduces jailbreak ASR from 86% to 4.4%. Next-gen
      version uses exchange classifiers (input+output context). Production
      approach that our method complements with discourse-level analysis.

  # ============================================================
  # Category 2: Multi-Turn Jailbreak Defenses (5 papers)
  # ============================================================

  - bibtex_key: deepcontext2026
    title: "DeepContext: Stateful Real-Time Detection of Multi-Turn Adversarial Intent Drift in LLMs"
    authors: "Anonymous"
    venue: "arXiv preprint"
    year: 2026
    arxiv: "2602.16935"
    category: multi_turn_defenses
    role: direct-competitor
    verified: true
    relevance_to_our_work: >
      PRIMARY POSITIONING TARGET. Uses RNN over BERT embeddings to track
      generic semantic drift. Achieves F1=0.84. DisPeD differs by grounding
      representations in persuasion strategy classification rather than
      generic semantics, arguing persuasion structure is harder to evade
      than semantic content (Pragmatic Evasion Asymmetry).

  - bibtex_key: tong2025biid
    title: "Bidirectional Intention Inference Enhances LLMs' Defense Against Multi-Turn Jailbreak Attacks"
    authors: "Tong et al."
    venue: "arXiv preprint"
    year: 2025
    arxiv: "2509.22732"
    category: multi_turn_defenses
    role: direct-competitor
    verified: true
    relevance_to_our_work: >
      Combines forward request-based intention inference with backward
      response-based retrospection. Significantly reduces ASR on both
      single-turn and multi-turn attacks. DisPeD differs by using
      persuasion-grounded embeddings rather than intention inference.

  - bibtex_key: gguard2025
    title: "An Attention-Aware GNN-Based Input Defender Against Multi-Turn Jailbreak on LLMs"
    authors: "Anonymous"
    venue: "arXiv preprint"
    year: 2025
    arxiv: "2507.07146"
    category: multi_turn_defenses
    role: direct-competitor
    verified: true
    relevance_to_our_work: >
      GNN-based approach modeling conversation structure as graph.
      Evaluated against Crescendo and ActorAttack. Represents structural
      approach to multi-turn defense; DisPeD uses sequential (GRU) rather
      than graph modeling of persuasion trajectories.

  - bibtex_key: safedream2026
    title: "SafeDream: Safety World Model for Proactive Early Jailbreak Detection"
    authors: "Anonymous"
    venue: "arXiv preprint"
    year: 2026
    arxiv: "2604.16824"
    category: multi_turn_defenses
    role: direct-competitor
    verified: true
    relevance_to_our_work: >
      World-model approach with CUSUM detection and contrastive imagination.
      Achieves early detection (1.06-1.20 turns before compliance). Shares
      our goal of early detection but uses latent safety state prediction
      rather than persuasion strategy grounding.

  - bibtex_key: bullwinkel2025repeng
    title: "A Representation Engineering Perspective on the Effectiveness of Multi-Turn Jailbreaks"
    authors: "Bullwinkel et al."
    venue: "arXiv preprint"
    year: 2025
    arxiv: "2507.02956"
    category: multi_turn_defenses
    role: foundation
    verified: true
    relevance_to_our_work: >
      CRITICAL MOTIVATION PAPER. Shows Crescendo keeps per-turn
      representations in "benign" region of representation space, explaining
      why per-turn defenses fail. This directly motivates DisPeD's approach
      of grounding representations in persuasion function rather than
      semantic content.

  # ============================================================
  # Category 3: Discourse Analysis in NLP (5 papers)
  # ============================================================

  - bibtex_key: mann1988rst
    title: "Rhetorical Structure Theory: Toward a Functional Theory of Text Organization"
    authors: "Mann and Thompson"
    venue: "Text & Talk"
    year: 1988
    category: discourse_analysis
    role: foundation
    verified: true
    relevance_to_our_work: >
      Foundational discourse theory. RST's hierarchical text organization
      informs our modeling of persuasion strategy sequences as structured
      discourse rather than bag-of-features.

  - bibtex_key: prasad2008pdtb
    title: "The Penn Discourse TreeBank 2.0"
    authors: "Prasad et al."
    venue: "LREC 2008"
    year: 2008
    category: discourse_analysis
    role: background
    verified: true
    relevance_to_our_work: >
      Major discourse annotation resource. PDTB's approach to annotating
      discourse relations at the connective level parallels our annotation
      of persuasion strategies at the turn level.

  - bibtex_key: stolcke2000dialogueact
    title: "Dialogue Act Modeling for Automatic Tagging and Recognition of Conversational Speech"
    authors: "Stolcke et al."
    venue: "Computational Linguistics"
    year: 2000
    category: discourse_analysis
    role: foundation
    verified: true
    relevance_to_our_work: >
      Foundational dialogue act classification using HMM over sequential
      turns. Our GRU-based persuasion trajectory modeling is a modern
      analogue of this sequential discourse structure approach.

  - bibtex_key: austin1962speechacts
    title: "How to Do Things with Words"
    authors: "Austin, J. L."
    venue: "Harvard University Press"
    year: 1962
    category: discourse_analysis
    role: foundation
    verified: true
    relevance_to_our_work: >
      Foundational speech act theory distinguishing locutionary,
      illocutionary, and perlocutionary acts. DisPeD operates at the
      illocutionary level (what the speaker intends to accomplish)
      rather than the locutionary level (what words are used).

  - bibtex_key: searle1969speechacts
    title: "Speech Acts: An Essay in the Philosophy of Language"
    authors: "Searle, J. R."
    venue: "Cambridge University Press"
    year: 1969
    category: discourse_analysis
    role: foundation
    verified: true
    relevance_to_our_work: >
      Extended Austin's speech act theory with systematic taxonomy.
      Our persuasion strategy taxonomy maps onto Searle's classification
      of illocutionary acts, providing theoretical grounding for
      treating persuasion as a functional category.

  # ============================================================
  # Category 4: Computational Persuasion Detection (4 papers)
  # ============================================================

  - bibtex_key: habernal2016convincingness
    title: "Which Argument Is More Convincing? Analyzing and Predicting Convincingness of Web Arguments Using Bidirectional LSTM"
    authors: "Habernal and Gurevych"
    venue: "ACL 2016"
    year: 2016
    category: computational_persuasion
    role: foundation
    verified: true
    relevance_to_our_work: >
      Pioneering computational persuasion work predicting argument
      convincingness from text. Establishes that persuasive properties
      are computationally detectable from language, supporting our
      premise that persuasion strategies are extractable from turn
      representations.

  - bibtex_key: tan2016winningarguments
    title: "Winning Arguments: Interaction Dynamics and Persuasion Strategies in Good-faith Online Discussions"
    authors: "Tan et al."
    venue: "WWW 2016"
    year: 2016
    category: computational_persuasion
    role: foundation
    verified: true
    relevance_to_our_work: >
      Analyzes persuasion dynamics in Reddit ChangeMyView. Shows timing,
      interaction patterns, and language features predict persuasion
      success. Supports our modeling of temporal persuasion trajectories
      as discriminative features.

  - bibtex_key: jaipersaud2025howdollmspersuade
    title: "How Do LLMs Persuade? Linear Probes Can Uncover Persuasion Dynamics in Multi-Turn Conversations"
    authors: "Jaipersaud et al."
    venue: "arXiv preprint"
    year: 2025
    arxiv: "2508.05625"
    category: computational_persuasion
    role: foundation
    verified: true
    relevance_to_our_work: >
      CRITICAL PRIOR WORK. Demonstrates persuasion dynamics are extractable
      from LLM turn-level representations via linear probes. Directly
      supports our premise that DeBERTa fine-tuned on persuasion taxonomy
      produces informative turn embeddings for trajectory modeling.

  - bibtex_key: cialdini2001influence
    title: "Influence: Science and Practice"
    authors: "Cialdini, R. B."
    venue: "Allyn & Bacon (4th edition)"
    year: 2001
    category: computational_persuasion
    role: foundation
    verified: true
    relevance_to_our_work: >
      Six principles of persuasion (reciprocation, consistency, social
      proof, liking, authority, scarcity). Our 8-class persuasion taxonomy
      maps partially onto Cialdini's principles, providing psychological
      grounding for the strategy classification.

  # ============================================================
  # Category 5: Jailbreak Attacks & Taxonomies (9 papers)
  # ============================================================

  - bibtex_key: zeng2024pap
    title: "How Johnny Can Persuade LLMs to Jailbreak Them: Rethinking Persuasion to Challenge AI Safety by Humanizing LLMs"
    authors: "Zeng et al."
    venue: "ACL 2024"
    year: 2024
    category: jailbreak_attacks_taxonomies
    role: foundation
    verified: true
    relevance_to_our_work: >
      CRITICAL PRIOR WORK. Proposes 40 persuasion techniques for
      jailbreaking (PAP), achieving >92% ASR. Establishes that persuasion
      is systematically used in jailbreaks. DisPeD operationalizes this
      observation into a detection system.

  - bibtex_key: russinovich2024crescendo
    title: "Great, Now Write an Article About That: The Crescendo Multi-Turn LLM Jailbreak Attack"
    authors: "Russinovich et al."
    venue: "USENIX Security 2025"
    year: 2024
    arxiv: "2404.01833"
    category: jailbreak_attacks_taxonomies
    role: foundation
    verified: true
    relevance_to_our_work: >
      Defines the Crescendo multi-turn jailbreak: gradual escalation
      through benign-seeming turns. Primary attack type in our evaluation.
      DisPeD detects the characteristic persuasion escalation trajectory
      that Crescendo relies on.

  - bibtex_key: chao2023pair
    title: "Jailbreaking Black Box Large Language Models in Twenty Queries"
    authors: "Chao et al."
    venue: "arXiv preprint"
    year: 2023
    arxiv: "2310.08419"
    category: jailbreak_attacks_taxonomies
    role: background
    verified: true
    relevance_to_our_work: >
      PAIR: automated iterative jailbreak refinement using attacker LLM.
      Represents the class of automated multi-turn attacks that DisPeD
      aims to detect through persuasion trajectory analysis.

  - bibtex_key: wei2023jailbroken
    title: "Jailbroken: How Does LLM Safety Training Fail?"
    authors: "Wei et al."
    venue: "NeurIPS 2023"
    year: 2023
    arxiv: "2307.02483"
    category: jailbreak_attacks_taxonomies
    role: foundation
    verified: true
    relevance_to_our_work: >
      Foundational jailbreak taxonomy: competing objectives and
      mismatched generalization. DisPeD addresses the mismatched
      generalization failure mode by operating at the pragmatic level
      where safety training has not yet generalized.

  - bibtex_key: hagendorff2026reasoning
    title: "Large Reasoning Models Are Autonomous Jailbreak Agents"
    authors: "Hagendorff et al."
    venue: "Nature Communications"
    year: 2026
    category: jailbreak_attacks_taxonomies
    role: foundation
    verified: true
    relevance_to_our_work: >
      CRITICAL MOTIVATION. Shows LRMs autonomously execute persuasive
      multi-turn attacks with 97% ASR using identifiable persuasion
      strategies. Directly supports our claim that the persuasion
      playbook is structurally necessary and therefore detectable.

  - bibtex_key: fitd2024
    title: "Foot In The Door: Understanding Large Language Model Jailbreaking via Cognitive Psychology"
    authors: "Anonymous"
    venue: "arXiv preprint"
    year: 2024
    arxiv: "2402.15690"
    category: jailbreak_attacks_taxonomies
    role: background
    verified: true
    relevance_to_our_work: >
      FITD jailbreak based on cognitive consistency theory. Progressive
      commitment escalation parallels Cialdini's consistency principle.
      One of three attack types in our evaluation (Crescendo, FITD,
      Deceptive Delight).

  - bibtex_key: deceptivedelight2024
    title: "Deceptive Delight: Jailbreak LLMs Through Camouflage and Distraction"
    authors: "Palo Alto Networks Unit 42"
    venue: "Palo Alto Networks Technical Report"
    year: 2024
    category: jailbreak_attacks_taxonomies
    role: background
    verified: true
    relevance_to_our_work: >
      Multi-turn jailbreak embedding unsafe topics among benign ones.
      65% ASR across 8 models in 3 turns. Third attack type in our
      evaluation, representing emotional manipulation strategy.

  - bibtex_key: ren2024actorattack
    title: "ActorAttack: Red-Teaming Large Language Models via Multi-Turn Actor Network Theory"
    authors: "Ren et al."
    venue: "ICLR 2025 submission"
    year: 2024
    category: jailbreak_attacks_taxonomies
    role: background
    verified: true
    relevance_to_our_work: >
      Multi-turn attack using actor-network theory to generate diverse
      attack paths. Achieves 84.5% ASR. Published SafeMTData dataset.
      Represents broader class of multi-turn attacks that exploit
      persuasion-like dynamics.

  - bibtex_key: zou2023gcg
    title: "Universal and Transferable Adversarial Attacks on Aligned Language Models"
    authors: "Zou et al."
    venue: "arXiv preprint"
    year: 2023
    arxiv: "2307.15043"
    category: jailbreak_attacks_taxonomies
    role: background
    verified: true
    relevance_to_our_work: >
      GCG: foundational gradient-based adversarial attack on LLMs.
      Represents the lexical-level attack that our evasion hierarchy
      positions as most easily detectable (vs. semantic vs. pragmatic).

  # ============================================================
  # Category 6: Red-Teaming (4 papers)
  # ============================================================

  - bibtex_key: perez2022redteaming
    title: "Red Teaming Language Models with Language Models"
    authors: "Perez et al."
    venue: "EMNLP 2022"
    year: 2022
    arxiv: "2202.03286"
    category: red_teaming
    role: background
    verified: true
    relevance_to_our_work: >
      Foundational automated red-teaming using LLMs to generate test
      cases. Establishes the paradigm of using models to find safety
      vulnerabilities, which multi-turn attacks like Crescendo extend.

  - bibtex_key: ganguli2022redteaming
    title: "Red Teaming Language Models to Reduce Harms: Methods, Scaling Behaviors, and Lessons Learned"
    authors: "Ganguli et al."
    venue: "arXiv preprint"
    year: 2022
    arxiv: "2209.07858"
    category: red_teaming
    role: background
    verified: true
    relevance_to_our_work: >
      Anthropic's large-scale human red-teaming study (38,961 attacks).
      Shows RLHF models are harder to red-team at scale. Provides context
      for why multi-turn persuasion-based attacks are increasingly
      important as single-turn attacks become less effective.

  - bibtex_key: mazeika2024harmbench
    title: "HarmBench: A Standardized Evaluation Framework for Automated Red Teaming and Robust Refusal"
    authors: "Mazeika et al."
    venue: "ICML 2024"
    year: 2024
    arxiv: "2402.04249"
    category: red_teaming
    role: background
    verified: true
    relevance_to_our_work: >
      Standardized red-teaming benchmark with 510 harmful behaviors.
      Used as evaluation framework by multiple jailbreak defense papers.
      Provides common evaluation vocabulary for our Related Work discussion.

  - bibtex_key: li2024mhj
    title: "LLM Defenses Are Not Robust to Multi-Turn Human Jailbreaks Yet"
    authors: "Li et al."
    venue: "arXiv preprint"
    year: 2024
    arxiv: "2408.15221"
    category: red_teaming
    role: foundation
    verified: true
    relevance_to_our_work: >
      CRITICAL MOTIVATION. Shows multi-turn human jailbreaks achieve >70%
      ASR against defenses with single-digit ASR on automated attacks.
      Directly motivates the need for multi-turn-aware defenses like DisPeD.

  # ============================================================
  # Category 7: Annotation Artifacts & Dataset Biases (4 papers)
  # ============================================================

  - bibtex_key: gururangan2018artifacts
    title: "Annotation Artifacts in Natural Language Inference Data"
    authors: "Gururangan et al."
    venue: "NAACL 2018"
    year: 2018
    arxiv: "1803.02324"
    category: annotation_artifacts
    role: background
    verified: true
    relevance_to_our_work: >
      Shows NLI datasets contain hypothesis-only artifacts enabling
      67% accuracy without premise. Directly relevant to our RC1
      (lexical shortcut concern): must ensure model learns persuasion
      trajectories, not surface-level artifacts.

  - bibtex_key: niven2019probing
    title: "Probing Neural Network Comprehension of Natural Language Arguments"
    authors: "Niven and Kao"
    venue: "ACL 2019"
    year: 2019
    category: annotation_artifacts
    role: background
    verified: true
    relevance_to_our_work: >
      BERT's 77% on argument reasoning entirely from spurious cues.
      Motivates our scrambled-label ablation (plan_003) to verify
      the model uses persuasion structure, not spurious correlations.

  - bibtex_key: poliak2018hypothesis
    title: "Hypothesis Only Baselines in Natural Language Inference"
    authors: "Poliak et al."
    venue: "StarSem 2018"
    year: 2018
    arxiv: "1805.01042"
    category: annotation_artifacts
    role: background
    verified: true
    relevance_to_our_work: >
      Systematic study of hypothesis-only artifacts across 10 NLI datasets.
      Motivates our approach to controlling for lexical confounds
      (TF-IDF analysis, register normalization) in jailbreak detection data.

  - bibtex_key: schuster2019debiasing
    title: "Towards Debiasing Fact Verification Models"
    authors: "Schuster et al."
    venue: "EMNLP 2019"
    year: 2019
    arxiv: "1908.05267"
    category: annotation_artifacts
    role: background
    verified: true
    relevance_to_our_work: >
      Claim-only classifiers perform competitively on FEVER without
      evidence. Parallels our concern that turn-level features alone
      (without trajectory modeling) may exploit dataset artifacts.

  # ============================================================
  # Category 8: Adaptive Attacks on Classifiers (2 papers)
  # ============================================================

  - bibtex_key: nasr2025attackermovessecond
    title: "The Attacker Moves Second: Stronger Adaptive Attacks Bypass Defenses Against LLM Jailbreaks and Prompt Injections"
    authors: "Nasr, Carlini et al."
    venue: "arXiv preprint"
    year: 2025
    arxiv: "2510.09023"
    category: adaptive_attacks
    role: foundation
    verified: true
    relevance_to_our_work: >
      CRITICAL FOR CLAIM 3. Bypasses 12 defenses with >90% ASR using
      adaptive attacks. BERT-based safety classifiers especially
      vulnerable. Motivates our theoretical argument that pragmatic-level
      features are harder to evade than lexical/semantic features
      (Pragmatic Evasion Asymmetry).

  - bibtex_key: andriushchenko2024adaptive
    title: "Jailbreaking Leading Safety-Aligned LLMs with Simple Adaptive Attacks"
    authors: "Andriushchenko et al."
    venue: "ICLR 2025"
    year: 2024
    arxiv: "2404.02151"
    category: adaptive_attacks
    role: background
    verified: true
    relevance_to_our_work: >
      100% ASR against aligned LLMs using simple random search on
      adversarial suffixes. Demonstrates that lexical-level attacks
      easily bypass safety training, supporting our evasion hierarchy
      (lexical < semantic < pragmatic).

  # ============================================================
  # Technical Foundation (1 paper)
  # ============================================================

  - bibtex_key: he2021deberta
    title: "DeBERTa: Decoding-enhanced BERT with Disentangled Attention"
    authors: "He et al."
    venue: "ICLR 2021"
    year: 2021
    category: technical_foundation
    role: foundation
    verified: true
    relevance_to_our_work: >
      Backbone model for DisPeD's turn encoder. Disentangled attention
      mechanism separates content and position representations, which
      we leverage for producing persuasion-aware turn embeddings via
      fine-tuning on 8-class strategy classification.

# Literature Map — persuasion_turn_jailbreak_detect
# Generated: 2026-05-17 by Paper Agent
# Target: EMNLP 2026 Main (ARR May cycle)
# Total entries: 39 (across 8 categories + technical foundation)
# All entries WebSearch-verified

metadata:
  project: persuasion_turn_jailbreak_detect
  target_venue: EMNLP 2026
  last_updated: "2026-05-17"
  total_papers: 39
  categories:
    - production_safety_systems
    - multi_turn_defenses
    - discourse_analysis
    - computational_persuasion
    - jailbreak_attacks_taxonomies
    - red_teaming
    - annotation_artifacts
    - adaptive_attacks
    - technical_foundation

papers:

  # ============================================================
  # Category 1: Production Multi-Turn Safety Systems (5 papers)
  # ============================================================

  - bibtex_key: inan2023llamaguard
    title: "Llama Guard: LLM-based Input-Output Safeguard for Human-AI Conversations"
    authors: "Inan et al."
    venue: "arXiv preprint"
    year: 2023
    arxiv: "2312.06674"
    category: production_safety_systems
    role: background
    verified: true
    relevance_to_our_work: >
      Foundational production safety classifier. Per-turn input/output guard
      that lacks multi-turn context modeling. DisPeD addresses this gap by
      modeling conversation-level persuasion trajectories.

  - bibtex_key: metallamaguard3_2024
    title: "Llama Guard 3"
    authors: "Meta AI"
    venue: "Meta AI (released with Llama 3.1)"
    year: 2024
    category: production_safety_systems
    role: background
    verified: true
    relevance_to_our_work: >
      Latest iteration of Llama Guard with multilingual support and tool-use
      safety. Still operates per-turn without multi-turn trajectory modeling.
      Baseline comparison target for production safety systems.

  - bibtex_key: zeng2024shieldgemma
    title: "ShieldGemma: Generative AI Content Moderation Based on Gemma"
    authors: "Zeng et al."
    venue: "arXiv preprint"
    year: 2024
    arxiv: "2407.21772"
    category: production_safety_systems
    role: background
    verified: true
    relevance_to_our_work: >
      Google's safety classifier suite (2B/9B/27B). Outperforms Llama Guard
      on public benchmarks. Demonstrates strong per-turn moderation but does
      not model multi-turn attack trajectories.

  - bibtex_key: han2024wildguard
    title: "WildGuard: Open One-Stop Moderation Tools for Safety Risks, Jailbreaks, and Refusals of LLMs"
    authors: "Han et al."
    venue: "NeurIPS 2024"
    year: 2024
    arxiv: "2406.18495"
    category: production_safety_systems
    role: background
    verified: true
    relevance_to_our_work: >
      Allen AI's multi-task safety moderator (prompt harm + response harm +
      refusal detection). Reduces jailbreak ASR from 79.8% to 2.4% on
      single-turn attacks, but multi-turn evasion path remains open.

  - bibtex_key: anthropic2025constitutional
    title: "Constitutional Classifiers: Defending against Universal Jailbreaks across Thousands of Hours of Red Teaming"
    authors: "Anthropic"
    venue: "arXiv preprint"
    year: 2025
    arxiv: "2501.18837"
    category: production_safety_systems
    role: background
    verified: true
    relevance_to_our_work: >
      Anthropic's defense using synthetically-generated training data from
      constitutional rules. Reduces jailbreak ASR from 86% to 4.4%. Next-gen
      version uses exchange classifiers (input+output context). Production
      approach that our method complements with discourse-level analysis.

  # ============================================================
  # Category 2: Multi-Turn Jailbreak Defenses (5 papers)
  # ============================================================

  - bibtex_key: deepcontext2026
    title: "DeepContext: Stateful Real-Time Detection of Multi-Turn Adversarial Intent Drift in LLMs"
    authors: "Anonymous"
    venue: "arXiv preprint"
    year: 2026
    arxiv: "2602.16935"
    category: multi_turn_defenses
    role: direct-competitor
    verified: true
    relevance_to_our_work: >
      PRIMARY POSITIONING TARGET. Uses RNN over BERT embeddings to track
      generic semantic drift. Achieves F1=0.84. DisPeD differs by grounding
      representations in persuasion strategy classification rather than
      generic semantics, arguing persuasion structure is harder to evade
      than semantic content (Pragmatic Evasion Asymmetry).

  - bibtex_key: tong2025biid
    title: "Bidirectional Intention Inference Enhances LLMs' Defense Against Multi-Turn Jailbreak Attacks"
    authors: "Tong et al."
    venue: "arXiv preprint"
    year: 2025
    arxiv: "2509.22732"
    category: multi_turn_defenses
    role: direct-competitor
    verified: true
    relevance_to_our_work: >
      Combines forward request-based intention inference with backward
      response-based retrospection. Significantly reduces ASR on both
      single-turn and multi-turn attacks. DisPeD differs by using
      persuasion-grounded embeddings rather than intention inference.

  - bibtex_key: gguard2025
    title: "An Attention-Aware GNN-Based Input Defender Against Multi-Turn Jailbreak on LLMs"
    authors: "Anonymous"
    venue: "arXiv preprint"
    year: 2025
    arxiv: "2507.07146"
    category: multi_turn_defenses
    role: direct-competitor
    verified: true
    relevance_to_our_work: >
      GNN-based approach modeling conversation structure as graph.
      Evaluated against Crescendo and ActorAttack. Represents structural
      approach to multi-turn defense; DisPeD uses sequential (GRU) rather
      than graph modeling of persuasion trajectories.

  - bibtex_key: safedream2026
    title: "SafeDream: Safety World Model for Proactive Early Jailbreak Detection"
    authors: "Anonymous"
    venue: "arXiv preprint"
    year: 2026
    arxiv: "2604.16824"
    category: multi_turn_defenses
    role: direct-competitor
    verified: true
    relevance_to_our_work: >
      World-model approach with CUSUM detection and contrastive imagination.
      Achieves early detection (1.06-1.20 turns before compliance). Shares
      our goal of early detection but uses latent safety state prediction
      rather than persuasion strategy grounding.

  - bibtex_key: bullwinkel2025repeng
    title: "A Representation Engineering Perspective on the Effectiveness of Multi-Turn Jailbreaks"
    authors: "Bullwinkel et al."
    venue: "arXiv preprint"
    year: 2025
    arxiv: "2507.02956"
    category: multi_turn_defenses
    role: foundation
    verified: true
    relevance_to_our_work: >
      CRITICAL MOTIVATION PAPER. Shows Crescendo keeps per-turn
      representations in "benign" region of representation space, explaining
      why per-turn defenses fail. This directly motivates DisPeD's approach
      of grounding representations in persuasion function rather than
      semantic content.

  # ============================================================
  # Category 3: Discourse Analysis in NLP (5 papers)
  # ============================================================

  - bibtex_key: mann1988rst
    title: "Rhetorical Structure Theory: Toward a Functional Theory of Text Organization"
    authors: "Mann and Thompson"
    venue: "Text & Talk"
    year: 1988
    category: discourse_analysis
    role: foundation
    verified: true
    relevance_to_our_work: >
      Foundational discourse theory. RST's hierarchical text organization
      informs our modeling of persuasion strategy sequences as structured
      discourse rather than bag-of-features.

  - bibtex_key: prasad2008pdtb
    title: "The Penn Discourse TreeBank 2.0"
    authors: "Prasad et al."
    venue: "LREC 2008"
    year: 2008
    category: discourse_analysis
    role: background
    verified: true
    relevance_to_our_work: >
      Major discourse annotation resource. PDTB's approach to annotating
      discourse relations at the connective level parallels our annotation
      of persuasion strategies at the turn level.

  - bibtex_key: stolcke2000dialogueact
    title: "Dialogue Act Modeling for Automatic Tagging and Recognition of Conversational Speech"
    authors: "Stolcke et al."
    venue: "Computational Linguistics"
    year: 2000
    category: discourse_analysis
    role: foundation
    verified: true
    relevance_to_our_work: >
      Foundational dialogue act classification using HMM over sequential
      turns. Our GRU-based persuasion trajectory modeling is a modern
      analogue of this sequential discourse structure approach.

  - bibtex_key: austin1962speechacts
    title: "How to Do Things with Words"
    authors: "Austin, J. L."
    venue: "Harvard University Press"
    year: 1962
    category: discourse_analysis
    role: foundation
    verified: true
    relevance_to_our_work: >
      Foundational speech act theory distinguishing locutionary,
      illocutionary, and perlocutionary acts. DisPeD operates at the
      illocutionary level (what the speaker intends to accomplish)
      rather than the locutionary level (what words are used).

  - bibtex_key: searle1969speechacts
    title: "Speech Acts: An Essay in the Philosophy of Language"
    authors: "Searle, J. R."
    venue: "Cambridge University Press"
    year: 1969
    category: discourse_analysis
    role: foundation
    verified: true
    relevance_to_our_work: >
      Extended Austin's speech act theory with systematic taxonomy.
      Our persuasion strategy taxonomy maps onto Searle's classification
      of illocutionary acts, providing theoretical grounding for
      treating persuasion as a functional category.

  # ============================================================
  # Category 4: Computational Persuasion Detection (4 papers)
  # ============================================================

  - bibtex_key: habernal2016convincingness
    title: "Which Argument Is More Convincing? Analyzing and Predicting Convincingness of Web Arguments Using Bidirectional LSTM"
    authors: "Habernal and Gurevych"
    venue: "ACL 2016"
    year: 2016
    category: computational_persuasion
    role: foundation
    verified: true
    relevance_to_our_work: >
      Pioneering computational persuasion work predicting argument
      convincingness from text. Establishes that persuasive properties
      are computationally detectable from language, supporting our
      premise that persuasion strategies are extractable from turn
      representations.

  - bibtex_key: tan2016winningarguments
    title: "Winning Arguments: Interaction Dynamics and Persuasion Strategies in Good-faith Online Discussions"
    authors: "Tan et al."
    venue: "WWW 2016"
    year: 2016
    category: computational_persuasion
    role: foundation
    verified: true
    relevance_to_our_work: >
      Analyzes persuasion dynamics in Reddit ChangeMyView. Shows timing,
      interaction patterns, and language features predict persuasion
      success. Supports our modeling of temporal persuasion trajectories
      as discriminative features.

  - bibtex_key: jaipersaud2025howdollmspersuade
    title: "How Do LLMs Persuade? Linear Probes Can Uncover Persuasion Dynamics in Multi-Turn Conversations"
    authors: "Jaipersaud et al."
    venue: "arXiv preprint"
    year: 2025
    arxiv: "2508.05625"
    category: computational_persuasion
    role: foundation
    verified: true
    relevance_to_our_work: >
      CRITICAL PRIOR WORK. Demonstrates persuasion dynamics are extractable
      from LLM turn-level representations via linear probes. Directly
      supports our premise that DeBERTa fine-tuned on persuasion taxonomy
      produces informative turn embeddings for trajectory modeling.

  - bibtex_key: cialdini2001influence
    title: "Influence: Science and Practice"
    authors: "Cialdini, R. B."
    venue: "Allyn & Bacon (4th edition)"
    year: 2001
    category: computational_persuasion
    role: foundation
    verified: true
    relevance_to_our_work: >
      Six principles of persuasion (reciprocation, consistency, social
      proof, liking, authority, scarcity). Our 8-class persuasion taxonomy
      maps partially onto Cialdini's principles, providing psychological
      grounding for the strategy classification.

  # ============================================================
  # Category 5: Jailbreak Attacks & Taxonomies (9 papers)
  # ============================================================

  - bibtex_key: zeng2024pap
    title: "How Johnny Can Persuade LLMs to Jailbreak Them: Rethinking Persuasion to Challenge AI Safety by Humanizing LLMs"
    authors: "Zeng et al."
    venue: "ACL 2024"
    year: 2024
    category: jailbreak_attacks_taxonomies
    role: foundation
    verified: true
    relevance_to_our_work: >
      CRITICAL PRIOR WORK. Proposes 40 persuasion techniques for
      jailbreaking (PAP), achieving >92% ASR. Establishes that persuasion
      is systematically used in jailbreaks. DisPeD operationalizes this
      observation into a detection system.

  - bibtex_key: russinovich2024crescendo
    title: "Great, Now Write an Article About That: The Crescendo Multi-Turn LLM Jailbreak Attack"
    authors: "Russinovich et al."
    venue: "USENIX Security 2025"
    year: 2024
    arxiv: "2404.01833"
    category: jailbreak_attacks_taxonomies
    role: foundation
    verified: true
    relevance_to_our_work: >
      Defines the Crescendo multi-turn jailbreak: gradual escalation
      through benign-seeming turns. Primary attack type in our evaluation.
      DisPeD detects the characteristic persuasion escalation trajectory
      that Crescendo relies on.

  - bibtex_key: chao2023pair
    title: "Jailbreaking Black Box Large Language Models in Twenty Queries"
    authors: "Chao et al."
    venue: "arXiv preprint"
    year: 2023
    arxiv: "2310.08419"
    category: jailbreak_attacks_taxonomies
    role: background
    verified: true
    relevance_to_our_work: >
      PAIR: automated iterative jailbreak refinement using attacker LLM.
      Represents the class of automated multi-turn attacks that DisPeD
      aims to detect through persuasion trajectory analysis.

  - bibtex_key: wei2023jailbroken
    title: "Jailbroken: How Does LLM Safety Training Fail?"
    authors: "Wei et al."
    venue: "NeurIPS 2023"
    year: 2023
    arxiv: "2307.02483"
    category: jailbreak_attacks_taxonomies
    role: foundation
    verified: true
    relevance_to_our_work: >
      Foundational jailbreak taxonomy: competing objectives and
      mismatched generalization. DisPeD addresses the mismatched
      generalization failure mode by operating at the pragmatic level
      where safety training has not yet generalized.

  - bibtex_key: hagendorff2026reasoning
    title: "Large Reasoning Models Are Autonomous Jailbreak Agents"
    authors: "Hagendorff et al."
    venue: "Nature Communications"
    year: 2026
    category: jailbreak_attacks_taxonomies
    role: foundation
    verified: true
    relevance_to_our_work: >
      CRITICAL MOTIVATION. Shows LRMs autonomously execute persuasive
      multi-turn attacks with 97% ASR using identifiable persuasion
      strategies. Directly supports our claim that the persuasion
      playbook is structurally necessary and therefore detectable.

  - bibtex_key: fitd2024
    title: "Foot In The Door: Understanding Large Language Model Jailbreaking via Cognitive Psychology"
    authors: "Anonymous"
    venue: "arXiv preprint"
    year: 2024
    arxiv: "2402.15690"
    category: jailbreak_attacks_taxonomies
    role: background
    verified: true
    relevance_to_our_work: >
      FITD jailbreak based on cognitive consistency theory. Progressive
      commitment escalation parallels Cialdini's consistency principle.
      One of three attack types in our evaluation (Crescendo, FITD,
      Deceptive Delight).

  - bibtex_key: deceptivedelight2024
    title: "Deceptive Delight: Jailbreak LLMs Through Camouflage and Distraction"
    authors: "Palo Alto Networks Unit 42"
    venue: "Palo Alto Networks Technical Report"
    year: 2024
    category: jailbreak_attacks_taxonomies
    role: background
    verified: true
    relevance_to_our_work: >
      Multi-turn jailbreak embedding unsafe topics among benign ones.
      65% ASR across 8 models in 3 turns. Third attack type in our
      evaluation, representing emotional manipulation strategy.

  - bibtex_key: ren2024actorattack
    title: "ActorAttack: Red-Teaming Large Language Models via Multi-Turn Actor Network Theory"
    authors: "Ren et al."
    venue: "ICLR 2025 submission"
    year: 2024
    category: jailbreak_attacks_taxonomies
    role: background
    verified: true
    relevance_to_our_work: >
      Multi-turn attack using actor-network theory to generate diverse
      attack paths. Achieves 84.5% ASR. Published SafeMTData dataset.
      Represents broader class of multi-turn attacks that exploit
      persuasion-like dynamics.

  - bibtex_key: zou2023gcg
    title: "Universal and Transferable Adversarial Attacks on Aligned Language Models"
    authors: "Zou et al."
    venue: "arXiv preprint"
    year: 2023
    arxiv: "2307.15043"
    category: jailbreak_attacks_taxonomies
    role: background
    verified: true
    relevance_to_our_work: >
      GCG: foundational gradient-based adversarial attack on LLMs.
      Represents the lexical-level attack that our evasion hierarchy
      positions as most easily detectable (vs. semantic vs. pragmatic).

  # ============================================================
  # Category 6: Red-Teaming (4 papers)
  # ============================================================

  - bibtex_key: perez2022redteaming
    title: "Red Teaming Language Models with Language Models"
    authors: "Perez et al."
    venue: "EMNLP 2022"
    year: 2022
    arxiv: "2202.03286"
    category: red_teaming
    role: background
    verified: true
    relevance_to_our_work: >
      Foundational automated red-teaming using LLMs to generate test
      cases. Establishes the paradigm of using models to find safety
      vulnerabilities, which multi-turn attacks like Crescendo extend.

  - bibtex_key: ganguli2022redteaming
    title: "Red Teaming Language Models to Reduce Harms: Methods, Scaling Behaviors, and Lessons Learned"
    authors: "Ganguli et al."
    venue: "arXiv preprint"
    year: 2022
    arxiv: "2209.07858"
    category: red_teaming
    role: background
    verified: true
    relevance_to_our_work: >
      Anthropic's large-scale human red-teaming study (38,961 attacks).
      Shows RLHF models are harder to red-team at scale. Provides context
      for why multi-turn persuasion-based attacks are increasingly
      important as single-turn attacks become less effective.

  - bibtex_key: mazeika2024harmbench
    title: "HarmBench: A Standardized Evaluation Framework for Automated Red Teaming and Robust Refusal"
    authors: "Mazeika et al."
    venue: "ICML 2024"
    year: 2024
    arxiv: "2402.04249"
    category: red_teaming
    role: background
    verified: true
    relevance_to_our_work: >
      Standardized red-teaming benchmark with 510 harmful behaviors.
      Used as evaluation framework by multiple jailbreak defense papers.
      Provides common evaluation vocabulary for our Related Work discussion.

  - bibtex_key: li2024mhj
    title: "LLM Defenses Are Not Robust to Multi-Turn Human Jailbreaks Yet"
    authors: "Li et al."
    venue: "arXiv preprint"
    year: 2024
    arxiv: "2408.15221"
    category: red_teaming
    role: foundation
    verified: true
    relevance_to_our_work: >
      CRITICAL MOTIVATION. Shows multi-turn human jailbreaks achieve >70%
      ASR against defenses with single-digit ASR on automated attacks.
      Directly motivates the need for multi-turn-aware defenses like DisPeD.

  # ============================================================
  # Category 7: Annotation Artifacts & Dataset Biases (4 papers)
  # ============================================================

  - bibtex_key: gururangan2018artifacts
    title: "Annotation Artifacts in Natural Language Inference Data"
    authors: "Gururangan et al."
    venue: "NAACL 2018"
    year: 2018
    arxiv: "1803.02324"
    category: annotation_artifacts
    role: background
    verified: true
    relevance_to_our_work: >
      Shows NLI datasets contain hypothesis-only artifacts enabling
      67% accuracy without premise. Directly relevant to our RC1
      (lexical shortcut concern): must ensure model learns persuasion
      trajectories, not surface-level artifacts.

  - bibtex_key: niven2019probing
    title: "Probing Neural Network Comprehension of Natural Language Arguments"
    authors: "Niven and Kao"
    venue: "ACL 2019"
    year: 2019
    category: annotation_artifacts
    role: background
    verified: true
    relevance_to_our_work: >
      BERT's 77% on argument reasoning entirely from spurious cues.
      Motivates our scrambled-label ablation (plan_003) to verify
      the model uses persuasion structure, not spurious correlations.

  - bibtex_key: poliak2018hypothesis
    title: "Hypothesis Only Baselines in Natural Language Inference"
    authors: "Poliak et al."
    venue: "StarSem 2018"
    year: 2018
    arxiv: "1805.01042"
    category: annotation_artifacts
    role: background
    verified: true
    relevance_to_our_work: >
      Systematic study of hypothesis-only artifacts across 10 NLI datasets.
      Motivates our approach to controlling for lexical confounds
      (TF-IDF analysis, register normalization) in jailbreak detection data.

  - bibtex_key: schuster2019debiasing
    title: "Towards Debiasing Fact Verification Models"
    authors: "Schuster et al."
    venue: "EMNLP 2019"
    year: 2019
    arxiv: "1908.05267"
    category: annotation_artifacts
    role: background
    verified: true
    relevance_to_our_work: >
      Claim-only classifiers perform competitively on FEVER without
      evidence. Parallels our concern that turn-level features alone
      (without trajectory modeling) may exploit dataset artifacts.

  # ============================================================
  # Category 8: Adaptive Attacks on Classifiers (2 papers)
  # ============================================================

  - bibtex_key: nasr2025attackermovessecond
    title: "The Attacker Moves Second: Stronger Adaptive Attacks Bypass Defenses Against LLM Jailbreaks and Prompt Injections"
    authors: "Nasr, Carlini et al."
    venue: "arXiv preprint"
    year: 2025
    arxiv: "2510.09023"
    category: adaptive_attacks
    role: foundation
    verified: true
    relevance_to_our_work: >
      CRITICAL FOR CLAIM 3. Bypasses 12 defenses with >90% ASR using
      adaptive attacks. BERT-based safety classifiers especially
      vulnerable. Motivates our theoretical argument that pragmatic-level
      features are harder to evade than lexical/semantic features
      (Pragmatic Evasion Asymmetry).

  - bibtex_key: andriushchenko2024adaptive
    title: "Jailbreaking Leading Safety-Aligned LLMs with Simple Adaptive Attacks"
    authors: "Andriushchenko et al."
    venue: "ICLR 2025"
    year: 2024
    arxiv: "2404.02151"
    category: adaptive_attacks
    role: background
    verified: true
    relevance_to_our_work: >
      100% ASR against aligned LLMs using simple random search on
      adversarial suffixes. Demonstrates that lexical-level attacks
      easily bypass safety training, supporting our evasion hierarchy
      (lexical < semantic < pragmatic).

  # ============================================================
  # Technical Foundation (1 paper)
  # ============================================================

  - bibtex_key: he2021deberta
    title: "DeBERTa: Decoding-enhanced BERT with Disentangled Attention"
    authors: "He et al."
    venue: "ICLR 2021"
    year: 2021
    category: technical_foundation
    role: foundation
    verified: true
    relevance_to_our_work: >
      Backbone model for DisPeD's turn encoder. Disentangled attention
      mechanism separates content and position representations, which
      we leverage for producing persuasion-aware turn embeddings via
      fine-tuning on 8-class strategy classification.

- Evidence: plan_006 cross-attack — Treatment=1.0, TF-IDF=0.94, Baseline=0.28 on DD
- Evidence: plan_004 perturbation (D012) — Treatment 0pp at K≥2, Baseline -12-15pp, TF-IDF -1.3pp(K≥3) to -9.6pp(K=1)
- Note: Treatment vs TF-IDF gap is small at K≥3 (1.3pp, n=76). Strongest claim is at K=1-2.
- Strength: strong empirical support across both OOD and perturbation dimensions

## Story Spine

**Problem**: Multi-turn jailbreak attacks (Crescendo, FITD, Deceptive Delight) distribute adversarial intent across individually benign turns. Bullwinkel et al. (2025) show per-turn representations are deliberately kept in a "benign" region, causing representation-level defenses to fail with a 50-point ASR gap. DeepContext (Su et al., arXiv 2602.16935, 2026) tracks generic semantic drift via RNN over BERT embeddings (F1=0.84) but confuses benign conversational evolution with adversarial manipulation.

**Gap**: Vanilla semantic temporal modeling (the natural approach: generic encoder + RNN over turn embeddings) catastrophically fails to generalize across attack types. DeepContext achieves F1=0.84 on in-distribution data but the approach collapses to F1=0.28 on unseen attack families. Production multi-turn guards (Llama Guard, WildGuard, ShieldGemma) and LLM-as-judge approaches detect individual harmful outputs but not the adversarial manipulation process. No published work uses persuasion-grounded fine-tuning to bridge this OOD generalization gap.

**Our angle**: DisPeD uses persuasion strategy classification as a multi-task fine-tuning objective, teaching the encoder to attend to attack-relevant pragmatic features shared across attack types. Aggregation over fine-tuned turn embeddings (mean pooling or GRU, both equivalent per plan_015) enables conversation-level detection. The persuasion objective provides an accessible supervision signal: even with imperfect (scrambled) strategy labels or binary labels, fine-tuning on persuasion-related text produces representations that generalize to unseen attacks (F1=1.0 on DD), while vanilla embeddings collapse (F1=0.28). The 8-class taxonomy additionally enables native interpretability through strategy trajectory analysis.

**Headline result**: "Vanilla semantic temporal modeling collapses on unseen attack types (F1=0.28 on Deceptive Delight). DisPeD, fine-tuned on persuasion strategy classification, achieves F1=1.0 on the same unseen attacks (+72pp). This generalization survives label scrambling (F1 drops only 1-6pp), confirming that the persuasion fine-tuning objective, not precise annotations, bridges the cross-attack OOD gap."

## Architecture

1. **Stage 1**: DeBERTa-v3-base fine-tuned on multi-task objective: 8-class persuasion strategy classification + binary jailbreak-intent classification
2. **Stage 2**: Aggregation (GRU or mean pooling, equivalent per plan_015) over DeBERTa [CLS] embeddings for conversation-level binary classification
3. **Baseline**: Same pipeline but with vanilla (not fine-tuned) DeBERTa embeddings
Note: plan_015 shows GRU ≈ mean pooling on both IID and OOD. Paper reports GRU as default architecture but ablation shows temporal modeling is not the source of improvement.

## Venue Fit Risks
- EMNLP 2026 LLM Security track: strong fit (dedicated track, high visibility)
- Discourse/Pragmatics reviewers may want more linguistic rigor: ground taxonomy in PAP (ACL 2024), Hagendorff (Nature Comm 2026), Cialdini principles, Speech Act Theory (Austin 1962, Searle 1969)
- Safety reviewers expect multiple attack types: need >= 2 attack families

## Anticipated Reviewer Concerns

### RC1: Lexical Shortcut (CRITICAL, must address pre-submission)
TF-IDF=1.0 IID and 0.94 OOD on DD. Lexical features are inherently strong for this task (D009). DisPeD cannot claim superiority over TF-IDF on raw detection performance alone.
- Mitigation strategy (post-D010): (a) acknowledge inherent lexical separability honestly; (b) DisPeD's primary value vs TF-IDF is interpretability (strategy trajectories, Claim 2) and bridging the vanilla temporal modeling gap (Claim 3); (c) plan_004 adversarial perturbation (pending): if TF-IDF degrades under paraphrasing but treatment doesn't, this demonstrates complementary robustness; (d) the core comparison that motivates DisPeD is vs vanilla DeBERTa+GRU (DeepContext approach, F1=0.28 on DD), not vs TF-IDF; (e) persuasion fine-tuning as supervision signal is the contribution, not beating a bag-of-words

### RC2: Small Dataset
480 samples is small for a detection paper.
- Mitigation: (a) statistical significance via bootstrap CI or paired tests; (b) cross-validation; (c) focus narrative on proof-of-concept for the principle, not SOTA numbers

### RC3: Single Attack Type (Crescendo Only)
Need generalization evidence.
- Mitigation: generate FITD-style and Deceptive Delight-style conversations using existing pipeline

### RC4: Strategy Label Quality (D010)
Scrambled-label control (D010) shows correct strategy labels contribute only 1-6pp to cross-attack F1. This is not a confound but a finding: the persuasion multi-task objective works as a supervision signal even with imperfect labels. The 8-class taxonomy's primary value is interpretability (Claim 2), not detection.
- Mitigation: report scrambled control results transparently; position taxonomy as practical training objective with interpretability bonus

### RC5: No Production/LLM-as-Judge Baseline (Dream-surfaced)
Without comparing against zero-shot LLM-based detection (e.g., GPT-4/Claude prompted for conversation-level jailbreak detection), practical positioning is unknown.
- Result: GPT-5.5 (frontier LLM) achieves F1=0.19-0.45 on Crescendo (precision=1.0, recall=0.11-0.29). Qwen3-8B F1=0.0-0.15. Both far below Treatment F1=1.0. GPT-5.5 is deceived by Crescendo's "surface educational framing," confirming that content-level analysis cannot detect persuasion dynamics. Unparseable rate 30-47% (increases with conversation length); paper must report this and provide unparseable-excluded upper bound. Even assuming best-case unparseable correction, LLM judge F1 ≈ 0.7-0.8, still far below Treatment=1.0. ✅ RESOLVED

### RC6: Interpretability Claims Without Human Eval
Strategy sequence outputs claimed interpretable but not evaluated.
- Mitigation: strategy transition matrix visualization + predicted-label trajectory analysis

### RC7: Related Work Inadequate (Dream-surfaced, THREE-TIER CONSISTENT)
~12 citations is far below venue norms (30-50). Missing coverage of: production safety systems (Llama Guard, WildGuard, ShieldGemma), LLM-as-judge, discourse analysis (RST, PDTB, dialogue acts), computational persuasion (Habernal & Gurevych 2016, Tan et al. 2016), red-teaming (HarmBench, Perez et al. 2022), annotation artifacts (Gururangan et al. 2018), adaptive attacks.
- Mitigation: expand to 30+ citations covering all missing categories (Paper Agent task)

### RC8: Incremental Novelty Over Prior Work (Dream-surfaced, TWO-TIER)
Pragmatic Evasion Asymmetry is a natural corollary of Zeng+Hagendorff+HowDoLLMs. Paper should position as "operationalizing known observations" not "identifying a new phenomenon."
- Mitigation: reframe contribution as operationalization + empirical validation (done in novelty positioning above)

### RC9: Multi-seed and Statistical Rigor (Dream-surfaced, THREE-TIER)
n=72 test set with single seed is inadequate.
- Result: 3-seed completed. Treatment F1=1.00±0.00 (zero variance), Baseline K=1 0.968±0.033. ✅ RESOLVED

### RC10: "None"-Collapse Ablation (Dream-surfaced, TWO-TIER)
Model may reduce to persuasion-presence detector rather than trajectory detector.
- Result: Confirmed (D013/D014). Binary≈9-class on DD (1-2pp gap). Mean pooling≈GRU. Model IS a persuasion-presence detector, not a trajectory detector. Paper acknowledges this honestly; 8-class value is interpretability only. ✅ RESOLVED (acknowledged)

### RC11: Lambda and Architecture Ablation (Dream-surfaced, TWO-TIER)
Lambda and architecture choices not ablated.
- Result: Lambda∈{0,0.3,0.5,2.0} all F1=1.0 (insensitive). Mean pooling≈GRU on IID and DD. Method robust to all hyperparameter/architecture choices. ✅ RESOLVED

## Scope Boundary
- IN: persuasion-mediated multi-turn attacks (Crescendo, FITD, Deceptive Delight, social engineering jailbreaks)
- OUT (acknowledged limitation): pure information accumulation attacks, token smuggling, single-frame roleplay

## Theoretical Grounding
### Core References
- Bullwinkel et al. (arXiv 2507.02956): per-turn representations kept "benign" by multi-turn attacks
- Speech Act Theory (Austin 1962, Searle 1969): existing detectors at locutionary act level, DisPeD at illocutionary act level
- PAP (Zeng et al., ACL 2024): 40 persuasion techniques for jailbreaking
- Hagendorff (Nature Communications 2026): identifiable persuasion strategies in 97% ASR attacks
- "How Do LLMs Persuade?" (arXiv 2508.05625): persuasion dynamics extractable from turn-level representations

### Must-Cite Categories (Dream-identified gaps)
- **Production safety**: Llama Guard 2/3, ShieldGemma, WildGuard, Constitutional Classifiers
- **Multi-turn defenses**: BIID, G-Guard, SafeDream
- **Discourse analysis**: RST (Mann & Thompson 1988), PDTB, dialogue act classification (Stolcke et al. 2000)
- **Computational persuasion**: Habernal & Gurevych 2016, Tan et al. 2016
- **Red-teaming**: Perez et al. 2022, Ganguli et al. 2022, HarmBench (Mazeika et al. 2024)
- **Adaptive attacks**: Nasr & Carlini et al. 2025
- **Annotation artifacts**: Gururangan et al. 2018, Niven & Kao 2019, Poliak et al. 2018
- **Jailbreak taxonomies**: Wei et al. 2024, Chao et al. 2023 (PAIR)

scope: global
tags:
  - workflow
  - research
  - planning
  - academic
version: 2
roles:
- agent
- paper_agent
---

## 触发条件

- 用户/Director 说"论文规划"/"paper plan"/"投稿计划"/"目标 NeurIPS/ICML/..."
- 核心方法验证成功后，主动建议制定论文计划
- 用户要求调整已有论文计划（重新生成 writing_plan.yaml）

## 产出

**唯一产出**：`projects/{name}/writing_plan.yaml` —— 所有下游 Worker（章节写作、画图、文献搜索）的共享合约。

文件格式见下方 §writing_plan.yaml 格式。生成后通过 `save_project_file("writing_plan.yaml", content)` 写入项目根目录。

## 步骤

### Step 1: 收集现状

1. `read_project_file("ideas.md")` — DECIDED（已验证）和 ACTIVE（待做）分区
2. `read_registry()` — 所有实验及状态、baseline 指标、metrics
3. `read_roadmap()` — 研究方向、实验矩阵、决策日志
4. `read_project_file("literature_map.yaml")` — 已有文献库（如存在）
5. `ls templates/latex/` — 确认目标 venue 模板可用性

### Step 2: 分析论文可行性（纯推理）

投稿门槛 mirror 自 `experiment-matrix` skill：

**投稿门槛（按 Director 指定的目标 venue 对标）**
- A 类（NeurIPS/ICML/ICLR）：3 个核心 contribution、主结果 ≥ 3 benchmark（含 ≥ 1 OOD）、Baseline ≥ 5、≥ 3 seed + 显著性、完整 ablation、≥ 1 efficiency、≥ 3 qualitative case
- 具体门槛由 Director 在审批 writing_plan 时把关，你只按 Director 指定的 venue 标准规划

**时间紧张时的应对（禁止降级目标 venue）**：
- 升级并行度：多 Worker 同时铺代码/数据/图表
- 砍低优先级维度（P2: efficiency/qualitative 可后补），集中火力在 P0 硬门槛
- 向 Director 汇报，由 Director 决定申请云 GPU 扩容或调整实验优先级
- **禁止自行建议更换目标会议**——venue 决策是 Director + 用户的权限

### Step 3: 模板选择

1. 查本地 `templates/latex/{venue}{year}/`
2. 缺失时 WebSearch 搜索官方最新模板，spawn Worker 下载到 `templates/latex/{venue}{year}/`
3. 仍找不到 → 复用最近版本（如 neurips2025），在 `meta.template_note` 标注原因
4. 在 `writing_plan.yaml` 的 `meta.template` 字段写入实际路径

### Step 4: 生成 writing_plan.yaml

按 §writing_plan.yaml 格式生成完整 YAML，包含：

- `meta`：venue/track/template/page_limit/deadline/core_claim/created_at
- `paper_outline`：各章节 word_budget + core_bullets + dependencies + 章节关联的 `tables`/`figures`/`registry_refs`/`citation_hints`
- `visualization_plan`：每张图的 fig_id/type/tool/data_source/placement
- `table_plan`：每张表的 table_id/caption/type/columns/data_source（§3.7 新增）
- `literature_strategy`：citation_budget + macro_context + micro_clusters
- `writing_order`：严格串行的章节写作顺序

**关键填写规则**：

- `visualization_plan.tool`：概念图（架构图/流程图）→ `paperbanana`；统计图（柱/线/热力）→ `matplotlib`

- `table_plan.data_source`：能从 registry 提取的写 `"registry: exp_xxx, exp_yyy"`；不能的写 `"manual"`

- `paper_outline.{section}.registry_refs`：该章节会引用的 exp_id 列表
- `writing_order`：先 Experiments、Method，再 Intro/Related Work，最后 Abstract/Conclusion

1. `save_project_file("writing_plan.yaml", yaml_content)` — 写入项目根目录
2. 向 Director 汇报摘要（投稿目标、core claim、章节数、图表数、引用预算）

## 1. Reliability Diagram（校准图）

**用途**：显示模型 confidence bin vs accuracy，对角线 = 完美校准。

```python
def plot_reliability_diagram(confidences, accuracies, n_bins=10,
                              label='', color='#0072B2',
                              title='Reliability Diagram',
                              outpath='reliability.pdf'):
    """
    confidences, accuracies: 各样本的 confidence 和 binary correct (0/1)
    """
    bin_edges = np.linspace(0, 1, n_bins + 1)
    bin_accs, bin_confs, bin_counts = [], [], []

    for i in range(n_bins):
        lo, hi = bin_edges[i], bin_edges[i+1]
        mask = (confidences >= lo) & (confidences < hi)
        if mask.sum() > 0:
            bin_accs.append(accuracies[mask].mean())
            bin_confs.append(confidences[mask].mean())
            bin_counts.append(mask.sum())
        else:
            bin_accs.append(float('nan'))
            bin_confs.append((lo + hi) / 2)
            bin_counts.append(0)

    bin_accs = np.array(bin_accs)
    bin_confs = np.array(bin_confs)

    fig, (ax_main, ax_hist) = plt.subplots(
        2, 1, figsize=(4, 4.5), gridspec_kw={'height_ratios': [3, 1]},
        sharex=True
    )

    # 主图：gaps
    ax_main.bar(bin_edges[:-1], bin_accs, width=1/n_bins, align='edge',
                color=color, alpha=0.7, label='Accuracy', zorder=2)
    ax_main.bar(bin_edges[:-1], bin_confs - bin_accs, width=1/n_bins, align='edge',
                bottom=bin_accs, color='red', alpha=0.3, label='Gap', zorder=2)
    ax_main.plot([0, 1], [0, 1], 'k--', linewidth=1, zorder=3, label='Perfect')
    ax_main.set_xlim(0, 1); ax_main.set_ylim(0, 1)
    ax_main.set_ylabel('Accuracy')
    ax_main.set_title(title)
    ax_main.legend(loc='upper left', fontsize=9)
    ax_main.grid(True, alpha=0.3, zorder=1)

    # ECE annotation
    ece = np.nansum(np.array(bin_counts) / sum(bin_counts) *
                    np.abs(bin_accs - bin_confs))
    ax_main.text(0.98, 0.02, f'ECE={ece:.3f}', transform=ax_main.transAxes,
                 ha='right', va='bottom', fontsize=9,
                 bbox=dict(boxstyle='round,pad=0.3', facecolor='white', alpha=0.8))

    # 直方图（样本密度）
    ax_hist.bar(bin_edges[:-1], bin_counts, width=1/n_bins, align='edge',
                color=color, alpha=0.5)
    ax_hist.set_ylabel('Count', fontsize=9)
    ax_hist.set_xlabel('Confidence')

    plt.tight_layout()
    plt.savefig(outpath)
    plt.close()
    print(f'Saved: {outpath}')
```

---
name: paper-plan
description: 论文规划——生成 writing_plan.yaml 作为下游 Worker 的共享合约（投稿目标、outline、可视化、表格、文献策略、写作顺序）。当 Director 说"写论文"/"准备投稿"/"论文计划"时使用。
scope: global
tags:
  - workflow
  - research
  - planning
  - academic
version: 2
roles:
- agent
- paper_agent
---

## 触发条件

- 用户/Director 说"论文规划"/"paper plan"/"投稿计划"/"目标 NeurIPS/ICML/..."
- 核心方法验证成功后，主动建议制定论文计划
- 用户要求调整已有论文计划（重新生成 writing_plan.yaml）

## 产出

**唯一产出**：`projects/{name}/writing_plan.yaml` —— 所有下游 Worker（章节写作、画图、文献搜索）的共享合约。

文件格式见下方 §writing_plan.yaml 格式。生成后通过 `save_project_file("writing_plan.yaml", content)` 写入项目根目录。

## 步骤

### Step 1: 收集现状

1. `read_project_file("ideas.md")` — DECIDED（已验证）和 ACTIVE（待做）分区
2. `read_registry()` — 所有实验及状态、baseline 指标、metrics
3. `read_roadmap()` — 研究方向、实验矩阵、决策日志
4. `read_project_file("literature_map.yaml")` — 已有文献库（如存在）
5. `ls templates/latex/` — 确认目标 venue 模板可用性

### Step 2: 分析论文可行性（纯推理）

投稿门槛 mirror 自 `experiment-matrix` skill：

**投稿门槛（按 Director 指定的目标 venue 对标）**
- A 类（NeurIPS/ICML/ICLR）：3 个核心 contribution、主结果 ≥ 3 benchmark（含 ≥ 1 OOD）、Baseline ≥ 5、≥ 3 seed + 显著性、完整 ablation、≥ 1 efficiency、≥ 3 qualitative case
- 具体门槛由 Director 在审批 writing_plan 时把关，你只按 Director 指定的 venue 标准规划

**时间紧张时的应对（禁止降级目标 venue）**：
- 升级并行度：多 Worker 同时铺代码/数据/图表
- 砍低优先级维度（P2: efficiency/qualitative 可后补），集中火力在 P0 硬门槛
- 向 Director 汇报，由 Director 决定申请云 GPU 扩容或调整实验优先级
- **禁止自行建议更换目标会议**——venue 决策是 Director + 用户的权限

### Step 3: 模板选择

1. 查本地 `templates/latex/{venue}{year}/`
2. 缺失时 WebSearch 搜索官方最新模板，spawn Worker 下载到 `templates/latex/{venue}{year}/`
3. 仍找不到 → 复用最近版本（如 neurips2025），在 `meta.template_note` 标注原因
4. 在 `writing_plan.yaml` 的 `meta.template` 字段写入实际路径

### Step 4: 生成 writing_plan.yaml

按 §writing_plan.yaml 格式生成完整 YAML，包含：

- `meta`：venue/track/template/page_limit/deadline/core_claim/created_at
- `paper_outline`：各章节 word_budget + core_bullets + dependencies + 章节关联的 `tables`/`figures`/`registry_refs`/`citation_hints`
- `visualization_plan`：每张图的 fig_id/type/tool/data_source/placement
- `table_plan`：每张表的 table_id/caption/type/columns/data_source（§3.7 新增）
- `literature_strategy`：citation_budget + macro_context + micro_clusters
- `writing_order`：严格串行的章节写作顺序

**关键填写规则**：

- `visualization_plan.tool`：概念图（架构图/流程图）→ `paperbanana`；统计图（柱/线/热力）→ `matplotlib`
- `table_plan.type`：`comparison` / `ablation` / `statistics` / `configuration`
- `table_plan.data_source`：能从 registry 提取的写 `"registry: exp_xxx, exp_yyy"`；不能的写 `"manual"`
- `paper_outline.{section}.tables` / `.figures`：把 `table_plan` / `visualization_plan` 的 id 关联到对应章节
- `paper_outline.{section}.registry_refs`：该章节会引用的 exp_id 列表
- `writing_order`：先 Experiments、Method，再 Intro/Related Work，最后 Abstract/Conclusion

### Step 5: 写入 + 确认

1. `save_project_file("writing_plan.yaml", yaml_content)` — 写入项目根目录
2. 向 Director 汇报摘要（投稿目标、core claim、章节数、图表数、引用预算）
3. 等待 Director 审批；如有调整，更新 writing_plan.yaml 重新提交

## writing_plan.yaml 格式

```yaml
meta:
  venue: NeurIPS 2026
  track: main
  template: templates/latex/neurips2026/   # Step 3 确认的实际路径
  template_note: ""                         # 复用旧模板时标注原因
  page_limit: 9
  deadline: 2026-06-15
  core_claim: "..."                         # 一句话核心 claim
  created_at: 2026-05-11T14:00:00Z

paper_outline:
  - section: abstract
    word_budget: 200
    core_bullets:
      - "问题：..."
      - "方法：..."
      - "结果：..."
    dependencies: [experiments, method]

  - section: introduction
    word_budget: 1200
    core_bullets:
      - "Hook: 一个具体、令人惊讶的事实"
      - "Gap: 现有方法的盲点（因为什么导致不够好）"
      - "Insight: 我们发现了什么别人没发现的东西"
      - "Mechanism: 基于 insight 我们做了什么不同的事"
      - "Contributions: [C1, C2, C3]"
    dependencies: [experiments]
    citation_hints:
      - "baseline X 引用原始论文"
      - "dataset Y 引用来源"
    figures: [fig1_overview]

  - section: related_work
    word_budget: 800
    core_bullets:
      - "Cluster 1: ... → 我们的区别"
      - "Cluster 2: ... → 我们的区别"
    dependencies: [introduction]

  - section: method
    word_budget: 1500
    core_bullets:
      - "Problem formulation"
      - "Proposed method"
      - "Theoretical justification"
    dependencies: []
    notation_table:
      X: "input features"
      Y: "target labels"

  - section: experiments
    word_budget: 2000
    core_bullets:
      - "Setup: datasets, baselines, metrics"
      - "Main results: Table 1"
      - "Ablation: Table 2"
      - "Analysis"
    dependencies: []
    registry_refs: [exp_001, exp_002, exp_003]
    tables: [tab1_main_results, tab2_ablation, tab3_hyperparams]
    figures: [fig2_main_results, fig3_ablation]

  - section: conclusion
    word_budget: 400
    core_bullets:
      - "Summary"
      - "Limitations (honest)"
      - "Future work"
    dependencies: [experiments, method]

visualization_plan:
  - fig_id: fig1_overview
    type: conceptual              # conceptual | statistical
    tool: paperbanana             # 概念图走 paperbanana
    description: "系统架构概览图"
    placement: introduction
    aspect_ratio: "16:9"

  - fig_id: fig2_main_results
    type: statistical
    tool: matplotlib              # 统计图走 matplotlib
    description: "主实验结果对比柱状图"
    data_source: "registry: exp_001, exp_002"
    placement: experiments
    aspect_ratio: "4:3"

  - fig_id: fig3_ablation
    type: statistical
    tool: matplotlib
    description: "Ablation 热力图"
    data_source: "registry: exp_003"
    placement: experiments

table_plan:
  - table_id: tab1_main_results
    caption: "Main experimental results on ..."
    placement: experiments
    type: comparison              # comparison | ablation | statistics | configuration
    columns: [Method, Dataset1, Dataset2, Dataset3]
    data_source: "registry: exp_001, exp_002, exp_003"
    notes: "加粗最优结果，次优下划线"

  - table_id: tab2_ablation
    caption: "Ablation study of ..."
    placement: experiments
    type: ablation
    columns: [Component, Metric1, Metric2]
    data_source: "registry: exp_004, exp_005"
    baseline_row: "Full model"    # ablation 基准行

  - table_id: tab3_hyperparams
    caption: "Hyperparameter settings"
    placement: experiments
    type: configuration
    columns: [Parameter, Value]
    data_source: "manual"         # 不从 registry 自动填充

literature_strategy:
  citation_budget: 40
  macro_context:
    - "large language model calibration"
    - "post-training quantization"
  micro_clusters:
    - cluster_name: "PTQ Methods"
      search_queries:
        - "post-training quantization LLM 2024 2025"
        - "GPTQ AWQ weight quantization"
      must_cite:
        - "GPTQ original paper"
        - "AWQ original paper"
      target_count: 8
    - cluster_name: "Calibration in NLP"
      search_queries:
        - "calibration large language models"
        - "temperature scaling neural networks"
      must_cite:
        - "Guo et al. 2017 calibration"
      target_count: 6

writing_order:                    # 严格串行，前序章节产出是后续章节的依赖
  - experiments
  - method
  - introduction
  - related_work
  - abstract
  - conclusion
```

## Story Arc（写作前必须回答）

在 `meta.core_claim` 中只写一句话核心 claim，但生成 writing_plan.yaml 前内部必须回答完整 Story Arc，并将关键答案分散到对应章节的 `core_bullets`：

1. **Hook**: 读者为什么应该关心？（具体、令人惊讶的事实/矛盾，不是泛泛"很重要"）→ Introduction 第一条 bullet
2. **Gap**: 现有方法的核心盲点是什么？（不是"不够好"，而是"因为 X 导致不够好"）→ Introduction
3. **Insight**: 我们发现了什么别人没发现的东西？→ 必须能回答；回答不上来说明还没准备好写
4. **Mechanism**: 基于 insight，我们的方法做了什么不同的事？→ Method
5. **Evidence**: 最强的一个数字是什么？→ Abstract / Experiments

## 禁止清单（写入 Worker prompt 时强制下传）

以下句式在全文禁止：
- "XXX has achieved remarkable success in recent years"
- "This demonstrates the effectiveness of our approach"
- "To the best of our knowledge, we are the first to..."
- "Extensive experiments demonstrate that..."

## 约束

- 时间线基于当前日期和 `meta.deadline` 倒推，按 AI 团队速度估 buffer：初稿 1-2 天（Paper Agent 全流水线）、内审 1 天（Reviewer 即时）、修订 1-2 天、提交准备 0.5 天。**不要按人类"初稿 2 周 + 内审 1 周"的节奏留 buffer**
- `paper_outline.{section}.registry_refs` 必须真实存在于 registry，引用未完成实验时在 `core_bullets` 标注 "[TODO exp_xxx]"
- `table_plan.data_source` 写明从 registry 哪些 exp_id 抽数，便于 Worker 后续 `write_paper_section` 时构建 provenance

## 1. Reliability Diagram（校准图）

**用途**：显示模型 confidence bin vs accuracy，对角线 = 完美校准。

```python
def plot_reliability_diagram(confidences, accuracies, n_bins=10,
                              label='', color='#0072B2',
                              title='Reliability Diagram',
                              outpath='reliability.pdf'):
    """
    confidences, accuracies: 各样本的 confidence 和 binary correct (0/1)
    """
    bin_edges = np.linspace(0, 1, n_bins + 1)
    bin_accs, bin_confs, bin_counts = [], [], []

    for i in range(n_bins):
        lo, hi = bin_edges[i], bin_edges[i+1]
        mask = (confidences >= lo) & (confidences < hi)
        if mask.sum() > 0:
            bin_accs.append(accuracies[mask].mean())
            bin_confs.append(confidences[mask].mean())
            bin_counts.append(mask.sum())
        else:
            bin_accs.append(float('nan'))
            bin_confs.append((lo + hi) / 2)
            bin_counts.append(0)

    bin_accs = np.array(bin_accs)
    bin_confs = np.array(bin_confs)

    fig, (ax_main, ax_hist) = plt.subplots(
        2, 1, figsize=(4, 4.5), gridspec_kw={'height_ratios': [3, 1]},
        sharex=True
    )

    # 主图：gaps
    ax_main.bar(bin_edges[:-1], bin_accs, width=1/n_bins, align='edge',
                color=color, alpha=0.7, label='Accuracy', zorder=2)
    ax_main.bar(bin_edges[:-1], bin_confs - bin_accs, width=1/n_bins, align='edge',
                bottom=bin_accs, color='red', alpha=0.3, label='Gap', zorder=2)
    ax_main.plot([0, 1], [0, 1], 'k--', linewidth=1, zorder=3, label='Perfect')
    ax_main.set_xlim(0, 1); ax_main.set_ylim(0, 1)
    ax_main.set_ylabel('Accuracy')
    ax_main.set_title(title)
    ax_main.legend(loc='upper left', fontsize=9)
    ax_main.grid(True, alpha=0.3, zorder=1)

    # ECE annotation
    ece = np.nansum(np.array(bin_counts) / sum(bin_counts) *
                    np.abs(bin_accs - bin_confs))
    ax_main.text(0.98, 0.02, f'ECE={ece:.3f}', transform=ax_main.transAxes,
                 ha='right', va='bottom', fontsize=9,
                 bbox=dict(boxstyle='round,pad=0.3', facecolor='white', alpha=0.8))

    # 直方图（样本密度）
    ax_hist.bar(bin_edges[:-1], bin_counts, width=1/n_bins, align='edge',
                color=color, alpha=0.5)
    ax_hist.set_ylabel('Count', fontsize=9)
    ax_hist.set_xlabel('Confidence')

    plt.tight_layout()
    plt.savefig(outpath)
    plt.close()
    print(f'Saved: {outpath}')
```

## 2. ECE Heatmap（方法 × 数据集 ΔECE）

**用途**：Main Results Table 的可视化版本，颜色 = ΔECE（红=恶化，蓝=改善）。

```python
def plot_ece_heatmap(delta_ece_matrix, methods, datasets,
                     title='ΔECE Heatmap (vs FP16)',
                     outpath='ece_heatmap.pdf'):
    """
    delta_ece_matrix: shape (n_methods, n_datasets), 正=ECE 恶化, 负=改善
    """
    import matplotlib.colors as mcolors

    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(len(datasets) * 1.2, len(methods) * 0.8 + 1))

    # 发散色图（中心=0, 红=恶化, 蓝=改善）
    vmax = np.nanmax(np.abs(delta_ece_matrix))
    norm = mcolors.TwoSlopeNorm(vmin=-vmax, vcenter=0, vmax=vmax)
    cmap = plt.cm.RdBu_r

    im = ax.imshow(delta_ece_matrix, cmap=cmap, norm=norm, aspect='auto')

    # 数值标注
    for i in range(len(methods)):
        for j in range(len(datasets)):
            val = delta_ece_matrix[i, j]
            if not np.isnan(val):
                color = 'white' if abs(val) > vmax * 0.6 else 'black'
                sign = '+' if val > 0 else ''
                ax.text(j, i, f'{sign}{val:.1%}', ha='center', va='center',
                        fontsize=9, color=color, fontweight='bold')

    ax.set_xticks(range(len(datasets)))
    ax.set_yticks(range(len(methods)))
    ax.set_xticklabels(datasets, rotation=30, ha='right')
    ax.set_yticklabels(methods)
    ax.set_title(title)

    cbar = plt.colorbar(im, ax=ax, fraction=0.046, pad=0.04)
    cbar.set_label('ΔECE (quantized − FP16)')
    cbar.ax.axhline(0, color='k', linewidth=0.8)

    plt.tight_layout()
    plt.savefig(outpath)
    plt.close()
    print(f'Saved: {outpath}')
```

## 3. T* Scatter Plot（任务 Regime 可视化）

**用途**：展示 5 个模型的 FP16 T* 分布，证明 Regime 跨模型一致性。

```python
def plot_tstar_scatter(tstar_data, outpath='tstar_scatter.pdf'):
    """
    tstar_data: dict of {model_name: {dataset: T*_value}}
    """
    DATASETS = ['HellaSwag', 'ARC-C', 'MMLU', 'BoolQ', 'TruthfulQA', 'NQ-Open']
    MODELS = ['LLaMA-3.1-8B', 'Qwen3-4B', 'Gemma-3-12B', 'Mistral-7B', 'Phi-3-mini']
    REGIME_BANDS = [
        (0, 1,    '#EBF5FB', 'Regime A\n(T*<1)'),
        (1, 5,    '#EAFAF1', 'Regime B\n(1≤T*<5)'),
        (5, 10.5, '#FDF2F8', 'Regime C\n(T*≥5)'),
    ]

    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 4))

    # 背景色区
    for lo, hi, color, label in REGIME_BANDS:
        ax.axhspan(lo, hi, alpha=0.25, color=color, zorder=0)
        ax.text(5.8, (lo + hi) / 2, label, va='center', fontsize=9,
                color='gray', zorder=1)

    model_colors = [COLORS.get(m.split('-')[0].lower(), '#333333') for m in MODELS]

    x = np.arange(len(DATASETS))
    for mi, (model, color) in enumerate(zip(MODELS, model_colors)):
        y = [tstar_data.get(model, {}).get(ds, np.nan) for ds in DATASETS]
        ax.plot(x, y, 'o-', color=color, label=model,
                markersize=7, alpha=0.85, zorder=2)

    ax.set_xticks(x)
    ax.set_xticklabels(DATASETS, rotation=15, ha='right')
    ax.set_ylabel('T* (FP16)')
    ax.set_ylim(0, 10.5)
    ax.set_title('Calibration Regime by Task — 5 Models (FP16)')
    ax.axhline(1, color='gray', linestyle='--', linewidth=0.8, alpha=0.5)
    ax.axhline(5, color='gray', linestyle='--', linewidth=0.8, alpha=0.5)
    ax.legend(loc='upper left', fontsize=9, ncol=2)
    ax.grid(True, alpha=0.2, axis='y', zorder=1)

    plt.tight_layout()
    plt.savefig(outpath)
    plt.close()
    print(f'Saved: {outpath}')
```
